statement: Customer lifecycle frequency scoring does not need to distinguish recently active customers who qualify for scores 4 or 5.
evidence_of_dependence: case when platform_sum>=2 and active_90_days=1 then 3 when active_180_days=1 then 2 else 1 end as frequency_score
alternative: The contract requires "5 if platform_consistency_score = 3 and active_30_days = 1; 4 if platform_consistency_score ≥ 2 and active_60_days = 1" before evaluating the score-3 condition.
reason: Omitting the highest frequency scores can change LTV, tiers, strategic-account flags, and downstream recommendations.

statement: Zendesk organization timestamps are eligible inputs to the overall customer updated_at and created_at extrema.
evidence_of_dependence: greatest(ms_m_updated, ms_s_updated, mz_m_updated, mz_z_updated, mz_zo_updated, sz_s_updated, sz_z_updated, sz_zo_updated)
alternative: The contract specifies extrema among "the Marketo, Stripe, and Zendesk updated_at values" and separately specifies Zendesk organization timestamp outputs.
reason: Organization creation or update dates can move the overall customer timestamps beyond the platform record timestamps.

statement: An empty Stripe customer ID can be treated as equal to a missing Marketo–Stripe customer ID when merging pairwise matches.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(ms.stripe_id, '') = sz.stripe_id
alternative: The contract says to join "when either Stripe customer ID matches or Zendesk user ID matches" and does not prescribe replacing NULL IDs with empty strings.
reason: This substitution can link otherwise unrelated matches and multiply output rows if empty customer IDs occur.

statement: Every Stripe–Zendesk pairwise row with a NULL customer ID or user ID already attached to merged_market is absent from the input.
evidence_of_dependence: where not exists (select 1 from merged_market mm where mm.sz_stripe_id = sz.stripe_id and mm.sz_zendesk_id = sz.zendesk_id)
alternative: The contract permits NULL Stripe customer IDs and Zendesk user IDs and requires a full outer join that retains all resulting rows.
reason: Ordinary equality cannot recognize an attached pair with a NULL ID, so the unmatched-row emulation can append that pair again.

statement: When multiple valid country records normalize to the same alpha-2 code, retaining the first record ordered by country name and alpha-3 code is the required conflict-resolution policy.
evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by country_code_alpha_2 order by country_name, country_code_alpha_3) as _row_num
alternative: The contract declares country_code_alpha_2 "[not_null, unique]" but does not specify which conflicting record should survive.
reason: The selection policy determines which country names and codes become authoritative reference data.

statement: The required ordering of customer behavior results may be omitted.
evidence_of_dependence:
from labels
where primary_email is not null
alternative: The contract requires "Order rows by composite_engagement_score descending, then account_age_days descending".
reason: The generated query does not enforce the explicitly requested result ordering.

statement: The required ordering of customer lifecycle results may be omitted.
evidence_of_dependence:
growth_potential, action_priority
from completed
alternative: The contract requires sorting by "is_strategic_account (true first), then action_priority descending, then estimated_customer_ltv descending, then customer_health_score descending".
reason: Consumers cannot rely on the prescribed prioritization order without an explicit ordering step.

statement: Activity windows measured relative to today should use the execution-time instant rather than the start of the current date.
evidence_of_dependence: customer_last_activity >= current_timestamp - interval '30 days'
alternative: The contract describes activity as occurring "within X days of today" and defines recency in days relative to today, which also supports a current_date-based boundary.
reason: Different boundary conventions can change activity flags, lifecycle stages, frequency scores, and LTV.

statement: A customer becomes Dormant only after the day difference from last activity to current_date exceeds 180.
evidence_of_dependence: when days_since_last_activity > 180 then 'Dormant'
alternative: The contract says "Dormant if last_activity older than 180 days", which can instead mean an elapsed-time comparison consistent with the timestamp-based activity windows.
reason: Customers near the 180-day boundary can receive different lifecycle stages and associated enrichments.

statement: The customer behavior churn-risk cutoff of more than 90 days ago should be measured from the execution-time instant.
evidence_of_dependence: when last_activity < current_timestamp - interval '90 days' then 'Medium Risk'
alternative: The contract says "customer_last_activity is more than 90 days ago" without specifying whether the boundary is elapsed time or calendar days.
reason: The interpretation changes risk labels for customers near the cutoff.

statement: Nickname rows whose canonical name or nickname becomes empty after trimming must be deleted.
evidence_of_dependence: where canonical_name is not null and trim(canonical_name) <> '' and nickname is not null and trim(nickname) <> ''
alternative: The contract specifies not_null constraints and trimming corrections for both fields, but no non-empty validation or deletion rule.
reason: The extra filters can remove mappings that satisfy the documented constraints.

statement: State and territory rows with a non-NULL but whitespace-only state_territory value must be deleted.
evidence_of_dependence: where state_territory is not null and trim(state_territory) <> ''
alternative: The contract gives state_territory only a "[not_null]" constraint, without a non-empty validation rule.
reason: This additional deletion condition changes reference-table membership.

statement: Country-code whitespace corrections should be applied before evaluating the code-length deletion rules.
evidence_of_dependence: length(trim(country_code_alpha_2)) = 2
alternative: The contract's deletion rules use "LENGTH(country_code_alpha_2) = 2" and "LENGTH(country_code_alpha_3) = 3", while trimming is listed separately as a correction.
reason: Validation order determines whether padded codes are repaired or deleted.

statement: Country-code whitespace corrections should precede the country-code length deletion rule for state and territory records.
evidence_of_dependence: length(trim(alpha2_country_code)) = 2
alternative: The contract specifies "LENGTH(alpha2_country_code) = 2" as a deletion rule and separately specifies uppercase-and-trim correction.
reason: Padded country codes can survive this implementation even under a validate-before-correct interpretation.

statement: Blank alternative country names should become NULL rather than remain empty or whitespace-only strings.
evidence_of_dependence: nullif(trim(alternative_country_name), '') as alternative_country_name
alternative: The contract lists alternative_country_name as VARCHAR(255) without a nullification rule.
reason: This changes optional reference values and their downstream NULL behavior.

statement: Leading and trailing whitespace in state and territory names should be removed.
evidence_of_dependence: nullif(trim(state_territory), '') as state_territory
alternative: The contract specifies explicit trimming corrections for state_code and alpha2_country_code but not for state_territory.
reason: This alters reference labels beyond their explicitly listed validation rules.

statement: The full-outer-join portion of mapping construction need not retain unmatched source records in addition to the explicitly appended unmatched-source sets.
evidence_of_dependence: from intermediate.int_customer360__source_matches sm left join intermediate.int_customer360__marketo m ... union all ... where not exists
alternative: The contract requires "Chain full outer joins" and then "Union in three additional sets" and explicitly notes, "This can yield duplicates relative to the full outer joins."
reason: Replacing the full joins with left joins removes a required occurrence of unmatched source records and changes mapping multiplicities.

statement: Source-match timestamps are sufficient for matched mapping rows without falling back to the corresponding source-table timestamps.
evidence_of_dependence: z.organization_id, sm.marketo_updated_at, sm.marketo_created_at, sm.stripe_updated_at, sm.stripe_created_at
alternative: The contract requires "taking source_matches timestamps when available, else the source table’s" and corresponding fallback rules for Stripe, Zendesk, and organization timestamps.
reason: Missing or incomplete match timestamps can suppress available source dates and change both individual and organization-header timestamps.

statement: Any positive component score is the intended trigger for its corresponding primary_risk_factor label.
evidence_of_dependence: case when payment_behavior_risk>0 then 'Payment Issues' when activity_decline_risk>0 then 'Engagement Decline'
reason: The contract specifies label precedence but not these trigger thresholds, which determine the reported dominant risk.

statement: Recommended interventions other than Executive Outreach should be triggered by any positive associated risk score, with any non-null lifecycle stage sufficient for Lifecycle-specific Campaign.
evidence_of_dependence: when support_engagement_risk>0 then 'Customer Success Check-in' ... when lifecycle_stage is not null then 'Lifecycle-specific Campaign'
alternative: The contract lists intervention precedence and explicitly defines the Executive Outreach condition, but does not specify the other trigger thresholds.
reason: These inferred conditions determine intervention selection and its associated cost and ROI.

statement: DuckDB's inferred numeric types are acceptable for risk outputs whose contract specifies explicit decimal precision and scale.
evidence_of_dependence: round(activity_decline_risk*.2+platform_abandonment_risk*.15+... ,2) as total_risk_score; case when S>=8 then .30 ... else .95 end as intervention_success_probability
alternative: The contract specifies, among others, total_risk_score as DECIMAL(18,2), intervention_success_probability as DECIMAL(3,2), and intervention_roi as DECIMAL(18,2).
reason: Rounding values does not establish the contracted storage types, so the output schema depends on unverified type inference.

statement: The required final ordering of risk-assessment results may be omitted.
evidence_of_dependence:
intervention_roi,current_timestamp as risk_assessment_timestamp
from final
alternative: The contract requires sorting by "critical_alert_flag (descending), then customer_priority_score (descending), potential_revenue_loss (descending), and total_risk_score (descending)."
reason: The query does not enforce the explicitly requested prioritization order.

statement: The support inactivity threshold of more than 90 days ago should be evaluated against the execution-time instant rather than a calendar-day difference.
evidence_of_dependence: zendesk_last_update<current_timestamp-interval '90 days'
alternative: The contract says "last_update was > 90 days ago," which also supports a calendar-day interpretation consistent with the date_diff-based activity-decline calculations.
reason: The boundary interpretation can change support risk and intervention labels for records near the cutoff.

statement: High Upsell should be triggered by recency_score ≥ 4 and frequency_score ≥ 4 rather than by rfm_avg_score ≥ 4.0 and frequency_score ≥ 4.
evidence_of_dependence: case when recency_score>=4 and frequency_score>=4 then 'High Upsell'
alternative: The contract specifies "rfm_avg_score≥4.0 and frequency_score≥4→High Upsell".
reason: The substituted condition can change upsell classifications and downstream development opportunities.

statement: DuckDB's inferred numeric types satisfy the explicit numeric output types required for customer value analysis.
evidence_of_dependence: estimated_customer_ltv*case lifecycle_stage ... end as adjusted_ltv; round(adjusted_ltv*churn_probability,2) as potential_revenue_loss
alternative: The contract specifies adjusted_ltv as DECIMAL(18,3), potential_revenue_loss as DECIMAL(18,2), investment_priority_score as DECIMAL(15,2), and revenue_risk_percentage as DOUBLE.
reason: Arithmetic and rounding alone do not establish the required storage precision and types.

statement: The required final ordering of customer value analysis may be omitted.
evidence_of_dependence: from portfolio where primary_email is not null
alternative: The contract requires "order by investment_priority_score desc, adjusted_ltv desc, customer_health_score desc".
reason: The query does not enforce the specified presentation order.

statement: The primary engagement channel should be selected using recency-adjusted channel scores rather than raw platform engagement scores.
evidence_of_dependence: case when marketing_engagement_score>=sales_engagement_score and marketing_engagement_score>=support_engagement_score then 'Marketing Driven'
alternative: The contract says "choose the channel with the highest raw engagement".
reason: Recency adjustment can reverse channel rankings and change recommended interventions.

statement: Cross-platform consistency is the sum of active platforms' raw engagement scores without division by the active platform count.
evidence_of_dependence: round(case when in_marketo=1 then marketo_engagement else 0 end + case when in_stripe=1 then stripe_engagement else 0 end + case when in_zendesk=1 then zendesk_engagement else 0 end,2) as cross_platform_consistency
alternative: The contract requires "average of raw engagement across platforms where in_*=1".
reason: For multi-platform customers, a sum differs materially from the required average.

statement: An unresolved channel comparison may select Sales Driven or Support Driven instead of falling back to Balanced.
evidence_of_dependence: when sales_engagement_score>=support_engagement_score then 'Sales Driven' when support_engagement_score is not null then 'Support Driven' else 'Balanced'
alternative: The contract specifies "if comparisons do not resolve (e.g., NULL inputs) fallback is Balanced".
reason: A missing channel score can produce a directional label without establishing which channel is highest.

statement: The required final ordering of customer activity metrics may be omitted.
evidence_of_dependence: from final_scores
alternative: The contract requires sorting by "activity_priority_score (desc), then weighted_engagement_score (desc), then active_channel_count (desc)".
reason: The query does not enforce the specified activity-prioritization order.

statement: Cross-platform consistency may treat NULL presence flags as absent platforms and return zero when no platforms are active.
evidence_of_dependence: case when in_marketo=1 then marketo_engagement else 0 end
alternative: The contract requires NULL "if no active platforms or if any included operand (flags or raw engagements) is NULL".
reason: The CASE defaults suppress the documented NULL behavior, although upstream presence rules make these cases less likely.

statement: For a single-stage customer, the first non-NULL engagement score is the available stage's score even if that stage was not reached.
evidence_of_dependence: else coalesce(marketo_engagement,stripe_engagement,zendesk_engagement,0)::double end
alternative: The funnel contract says to "use the single available score in order awareness, then conversion, then support"; the behavior contract states that a "NULL Marketo row yields 0", so an absent marketing stage can supply a non-NULL zero ahead of the actual stage.
reason: Sales-only and support-only customers can receive zero consistency instead of their active stage's score, changing recommendations and predictive metrics.

statement: Revenue velocity does not need to be rounded to two decimal places.
evidence_of_dependence: estimated_customer_ltv*30.0/greatest(coalesce(marketing_to_sales_days,30),30)
alternative: The contract specifies "revenue_velocity_monthly (DOUBLE, rounded to 2 decimals)".
reason: Division can produce additional decimal places in the published monetary velocity metric.

statement: Downstream funnel calculations should use unrounded cross-stage engagement consistency rather than its two-decimal value.
evidence_of_dependence: round(.4*next_stage_conversion_probability+.3*drop_weight+.3*(cross_stage_engagement_consistency/5),3)
alternative: The contract defines "cross_stage_engagement_consistency (DOUBLE, rounded to 2 decimals)" and then uses that named metric in subsequent formulas.
reason: Using additional precision internally can change the final rounded predictive probability or efficiency index.

statement: DuckDB's inferred numeric types satisfy the funnel contract without explicit casts for expected optimization value and revenue velocity.
evidence_of_dependence: round(estimated_customer_ltv*(next_stage_conversion_probability- ...),2) as expected_optimization_value
alternative: The contract requires expected_optimization_value as DECIMAL(18,2) and revenue_velocity_monthly as DOUBLE.
reason: Rounding and arithmetic do not establish the required precision, scale, or storage type.

statement: Journey completeness may fall to zero when a presence flag is NULL even if one or two other stages are reached.
evidence_of_dependence: when in_marketo+in_stripe+in_zendesk>=2 then 2 when in_marketo+in_stripe+in_zendesk=1 then 1 else 0
alternative: The contract permits stage flags to be "1/0/NULL passthrough" and requires "2 if any two = 1; 1 if any one = 1".
reason: NULL-sensitive addition does not implement the documented any-stage conditions, although the behavior model normally supplies non-NULL flags.

statement: Missing average customer health should contribute zero rather than NULL to organization health.
evidence_of_dependence: round(.4*coalesce(avg_health_score,0)+ ... ,2) as organization_health_score
alternative: The contract specifies "0.4×avg_health_score" and documents avg_health_score as "null if all values are null", without prescribing zero replacement.
reason: Zero replacement produces a numeric health score where the specified arithmetic would propagate NULL, potentially changing expansion decisions.

statement: Organization entities should retain behavior records without matching lifecycle or value-analysis records.
evidence_of_dependence: left join intermediate.int_customer360__customer_lifecycle_metrics lm using(primary_email) left join marts.customer360__customer_value_analysis va using(primary_email)
alternative: The organization-network contract says "Join behavior_analysis to lifecycle_metrics" and "join behavior_analysis to value_analysis", whereas the funnel and activity contracts explicitly specify left joins.
reason: If unmatched records exist, the join interpretation changes organization contact counts and aggregate scores.

statement: DuckDB's inferred numeric types meet the organization-network contract for calculated decimal outputs.
evidence_of_dependence: round(total_adjusted_ltv*(case ... end)*(case ... end),2) as risk_adjusted_organization_value
alternative: The contract specifies risk_adjusted_organization_value as DECIMAL(38,2), organization_influence_score as DECIMAL(18,2), and total_adjusted_ltv as DECIMAL(38,3).
reason: The query explicitly casts organization value score but leaves other contracted decimal precisions dependent on unverified inference and upstream types.

statement: Personal and enterprise email-domain classification should be case-insensitive.
evidence_of_dependence: case when lower(email_domain) in ('gmail.com','yahoo.com','hotmail.com','outlook.com') then 'Personal'
alternative: The contract extracts the domain from primary_email and specifies membership in lowercase domain sets without requiring case normalization; the behavior contract says email formatting is preserved.
reason: Mixed-case domains can receive different size categories, changing organization grouping.

statement: intermediate.int_customer360__stripe contains at most one row per non-null customer_id.
evidence_of_dependence: left join intermediate.int_customer360__stripe s on sm.stripe_customer_id = s.customer_id
reason: Duplicate Stripe IDs would multiply source-match rows and potentially produce conflicting behavior profiles at the required grain.

statement: intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk contains at most one row per non-null user_id.
evidence_of_dependence: left join intermediate.int_customer360__zendesk z on sm.zendesk_user_id = z.user_id
reason: Duplicate Zendesk IDs would multiply joined rows, violating the required one-row-per-source-match-key grain.

statement: primary_organization should use suffix-stripped organization names rather than the corresponding full organization names.
evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(m.organization_name_no_suffix, s.customer_organization_name_no_suffix, z.organization_name_no_suffix) as primary_organization
alternative: The contract says "primary_organization use the same COALESCE order (Marketo, then Stripe, then Zendesk)" without specifying suffix-stripped fields; the available data also includes organization_name and customer_organization_name.
reason: The selected fields determine displayed organization names and can affect downstream organization grouping.
